answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by forcing each new identity to lock a refundable bond that only unlocks after established peers attest to genuine work across several epochs. Like water slowly carving a karst of verifiable history, real reputation seeps through narrow, auditable channels, while a plume of cheap clones spawned at once drains its collateral fast. Every attestation is signed with a distinct quill, so near-identical identities get flagged and slashed before they can sway a vote.
